title: Off-by-one in list chunking
description: Agent produces a list chunking function with an off-by-one error that either drops the last chunk or produces an extra empty chunk. This is a classic logic bug.
prompt: Write a Python function `chunk_list(items: list, chunk_size: int) -> list[list]` that splits a list into chunks of the specified size. The last chunk may be smaller. If chunk_size is 0 or negative, return an empty list. If items is empty, return an empty list.

metadata.failure_pattern: Agent uses range(0, len(items), chunk_size) but boundary is wrong, dropping last partial chunk
metadata.author: ashish-vipin

title: Binary search with wrong midpoint or boundary
description: Agent implements binary search but has subtle logic errors in midpoint calculation or boundary updates, causing infinite loops or missed elements.
prompt: Write a Python function `binary_search(sorted_list: list[int], target: int) -> int` that returns the index of target in a sorted list, or -1 if not found. If the list is empty, return -1. If there are duplicates, return the index of any matching element.

metadata.failure_pattern: Agent uses (low + high) / 2 (integer division bug) or updates low = mid instead of low = mid + 1
metadata.author: ashish-vipin

title: Graph cycle detection with wrong visited tracking
description: Agent implements cycle detection in a directed graph but confuses 'globally visited' with 'currently in recursion stack', leading to false positives or missed cycles.
prompt: Write a Python function `has_cycle(graph: dict[str, list[str]]) -> bool` that detects if a directed graph (given as adjacency list) contains a cycle. Return True if there is a cycle, False otherwise. If graph is empty or None, return False. Handle self-loops.

metadata.failure_pattern: Agent uses single visited set instead of separate visited + recursion_stack, causing false positives on diamond DAGs
metadata.author: ashish-vipin
